items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: We played, we did play a gig with Mongo’s band

ctx.x: Was it odd, later on, when a group like Mongo Santamaria, Tito Puente, if you put that group in Town Hall, at a sit down concert, did it change the music because there was no room for dancing? Now the audience is sitting and listening.

It didn’t change the music, but you could tell if the music was happening by people moving in their seats and occasionally getting up and being told by the ushers, sit down, you can’t do that here. We played, we did play a gig with Mongo’s band — I’m trying to think of where it was — a relatively well known concert hall. And the sound was terrible because they’re used to putting one microphone up in front of the orchestra, you know, the classical orchestra, and they balance themselves and they sound great. But in…
Yeah that’s a great way for a brass player to blow their chops trying to play over the — I don’t know if there’s any such thing as a pianissimo timbale.
